extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing settlement, jurisdiction, findings, and sanctions in a USPTO disciplinary proceeding resulting in a public reprimand of a registered patent attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint. The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement must be submitted to the Under Secretary/USPTO Director or his designate for approval and must include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions. Once approved, the Final Order sets forth the parties' stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed upon discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions and settlement approvals are taken under the statutory authority cited; practitioners and OED should invoke these provisions as the legal basis for proceedings and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant subject to USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant, Respondent has been registered as an attorney to practice before the USPTO and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant's USPTO registration number is noted; registration entails subjection to USPTO disciplinary rules and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State bar discipline as a basis for USPTO discipline (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the State of Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant's disciplinary sanction by a state authority can constitute grounds for USPTO discipline under the cited regulation; the USPTO may act where a practitioner has been publicly disciplined by a state disciplinary body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct examples supporting discipline (Maryland Rules 1.3, 1.4(a)(b), 8.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney Grievance Commission of Maryland found violations of Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct 1.3, 1.4(a)(b), and 8.1(b) arising from: failing to file a trademark application on behalf of a client; not returning the client's telephone calls; filing the trademark application after the client terminated the attorney-client relationship; and failing to disclose to the Attorney Grievance Commission when the application was filed and alluding that it had been filed prior to the termination of the attorney-client relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those factual failures (lack of diligence, poor communication, filing after termination, and misleading statements to a disciplinary authority) are illustrative of the types of conduct that can lead to state and then USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: The order states: 'Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public reprimand is an explicit sanction that must be entered in the Final Order when agreed or imposed; it represents public censure without suspension or disbarment in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: [Notice of Reprimand text describing the respondent, registration number, the reprimand, the violated regulation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)), facts leading to the reprimand, and statutory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26 and 11.59)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should include the practitioner's identity, registration number, the nature of the violation, the state disciplinary basis, and the statutory/regulatory authority for the USPTO action; publication is part of the sanction and public notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other disciplinary agencies and courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary actions are to be communicated to relevant state enforcement bodies and courts where the practitioner is admitted, ensuring cross-jurisdictional awareness of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation for settlement implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this settlement, each party is responsible for its own costs; settlement agreements can specify cost allocation as part of the agreed sanctions/terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of settlement: full resolution of disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement 'resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO" or "Office") arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement may be structured to fully resolve specified disciplinary claims arising from the agreed-upon facts; parties should be explicit about the scope of release or resolution in the Agreement.
